notes: These evals test the TICK DECISION behavior plus the recovery/stop substrate. A real tick needs live GitHub state and the Cron tools, so each prompt hands the model a concrete slot + provider state and asks for the step-by-step plan it would execute; assertions check the plan takes the branch the contract mandates. Cases 0–10 cover per-tick dispatch/idle decisions; cases 11–17 cover cron-delivered ticks handing back to the token-free monitor, the owner stop switch, and the stopped-slot / kill-file absorb that makes an unreachable orphaned cron inert. Run via skill-creator's eval runner — CI does not execute these (ci.yml gates on vitest/check-skill-deps; skill-eval.yml runs gate scenarios sourced from muggle-ai-brain and the routing eval).

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr500 500. The slot is open. The PR has two unresolved, not-outdated review threads whose newest comments are from a human (no muggle-do:bot marker), CI is fully green, and the branch is level with master. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: computes_actionable_from_live_thread_state
assertions.text: Plan derives the actionable set from current unresolved-thread state, not from a stored review-id cursor.

assertions.name: classifies_by_loop_marker
assertions.text: Plan decides a thread is actionable by the absence of the muggle-do:bot marker on the newest comment, never by author login.

assertions.name: cancels_own_cron_before_dispatch
assertions.text: Plan cancels this watcher's own cron before dispatching, so no tick overlaps the running cycle.

assertions.name: dispatches_address_reviews
assertions.text: Plan dispatches /muggle-do with an address-reviews directive carrying the PR URL, slug, and owning review ids, then exits.

assertions.name: stays_a_dumb_pipe
assertions.text: Plan does NOT classify reviews, post replies, resolve threads, or escalate — those belong to /muggle-do.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr501 501. The slot is open. There is one unresolved human review thread AND two red required checks on the head SHA. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: dispatches_address_reviews_only
assertions.text: Plan dispatches address-reviews for the review thread.

assertions.name: does_not_poll_or_dispatch_ci
assertions.text: Plan does NOT dispatch fix-ci on this tick — actionable feedback preempts the CI branch entirely.

assertions.name: single_dispatch_then_exit
assertions.text: Plan performs exactly one dispatch and exits rather than handling both concerns in one tick.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr502 502. The slot is open, there are no unresolved review threads, CI is green. GitHub reports mergeStateStatus BLOCKED and mergeable MERGEABLE, and the compare call shows behind_by 4. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: reads_staleness_from_compare
assertions.text: Plan determines the branch is out of date from behind_by on the compare call (commit ancestry).

assertions.name: does_not_trust_mergeStateStatus
assertions.text: Plan does NOT conclude the branch is current just because mergeStateStatus reads BLOCKED rather than BEHIND.

assertions.name: dispatches_rebase
assertions.text: Plan dispatches /muggle-do with a rebase directive (PR URL + slug, no review ids, no check names).

assertions.name: keys_dedup_on_head_and_base_pair
assertions.text: Plan keys the rebase attempt/escalation lookup on the head..base_tip pair, not the head SHA alone.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr503 503. The slot is open, no unresolved review threads, branch is level with its base. Two checks are red on the head SHA. ci_fix_attempts for that SHA is 1 and the SHA is not in ci_escalated_shas. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: checks_attempt_budget
assertions.text: Plan verifies ci_fix_attempts for the head SHA is under the cap of 3 before dispatching.

assertions.name: checks_escalated_set
assertions.text: Plan verifies the head SHA is not in ci_escalated_shas.

assertions.name: dispatches_fix_ci_with_check_names
assertions.text: Plan dispatches /muggle-do with a fix-ci directive carrying the red check names.

assertions.name: cancels_own_cron_before_dispatch
assertions.text: Plan cancels this watcher's cron before dispatching.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr504 504. The slot is open, no unresolved review threads, branch is level with its base. Three checks are red on the head SHA, ci_fix_attempts for that SHA is 3, and the SHA is in ci_escalated_shas. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: does_not_dispatch
assertions.text: Plan does NOT dispatch fix-ci — the budget is spent and the SHA is already escalated.

assertions.name: treats_as_durable_block
assertions.text: Plan classifies this idle as blocked pending a human (reason ci_escalated), not as a transient idle.

assertions.name: reminds_owner_at_1m
assertions.text: Plan emits a one-line owner reminder and keeps the normal 1m cadence — it does not back off, slow down, or stop polling.

assertions.name: no_pr_side_post
assertions.text: Plan does NOT post anything to the PR for a blocked tick; the reminder goes to the loop owner in-session.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr505 505. Refreshing the PR shows state MERGED. The slot on disk still says open. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: finalizes_the_slot
assertions.text: Plan finalizes the slot: marks it terminal, writes result.md, logs, and unschedules this watcher's cron.

assertions.name: does_not_respawn
assertions.text: Plan does NOT respawn or re-arm a watcher — a terminal PR needs none.

assertions.name: hands_off_terminal_wrapup
assertions.text: Plan hands the terminal wrap-up to /muggle-do post-merge cleanup as the turn's last action.

assertions.name: unschedules_recorded_id_first
assertions.text: Plan cancels the cron by the id recorded in cron.json first, falling back to a CronList match — so teardown works even after CronList has gone blind.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr506 506. Reading the slot, prs.json already records state merged and result.md exists — this fire was queued before the cron was cancelled. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: detects_stale_fire
assertions.text: Plan recognises this as a stale queued fire from the on-disk terminal state before fetching anything.

assertions.name: does_not_refetch_or_refinalize
assertions.text: Plan does NOT re-fetch the PR, re-write result.md, or re-run the terminal handoff.

assertions.name: defensively_cancels_and_logs
assertions.text: Plan defensively cancels any lingering cron for the slug and appends a stale-tick line to followup.log, then exits.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr507 507. prs.json records state merged and result.md exists. followup.log already holds four stale-tick lines for this slot and no stale-orphan-escalated line. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: detects_orphaned_cron
assertions.text: Plan concludes the cron is orphaned — repeated stale fires after finalize mean both cancel-cron lookups (recorded id, CronList match) keep missing it — rather than treating this as a normal queued-fire drain.

assertions.name: escalates_to_owner_once
assertions.text: Plan surfaces a one-line owner notice that only a session restart clears the orphan, and appends a stale-orphan-escalated marker line so the notice never repeats.

assertions.name: later_fires_absorb_silently
assertions.text: Plan treats any stale fire after the marker exists as a silent absorb — log stale-tick and exit, no repeated notice.

assertions.name: never_guess_deletes_other_ids
assertions.text: Plan does NOT delete cron ids that CronList surfaces for other slugs — those belong to other live watchers.

evals.prompt: Arm the watch for muggle-ai-works-pr508 508 after a clean drain (no reviews, no unresolved threads, checks green at seed time). Describe the watch.sh monitor loop you would write and what makes it wake the session.

assertions.name: polls_check_run_rollup
assertions.text: The loop polls the head SHA's check-run rollup each iteration, not just reviews and threads.

assertions.name: wakes_only_on_settled_red
assertions.text: The loop wakes the session when the checks have settled with a failure (no check pending and one or more in the fail bucket) — it does NOT wake while any check is still pending.

assertions.name: dedups_ci_on_head_sha
assertions.text: The loop dedups the CI wake on the head SHA (fires once per red head) rather than on a monotonic id, because the check rollup is non-monotonic and resets on each push.

assertions.name: stays_a_dumb_pipe
assertions.text: The loop only signals that CI went red and hands off to a tick; it does NOT apply the ci_fix_attempts budget, classify the failure, or dispatch fix-ci itself — those belong to the tick and /muggle-do.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr509 509. The slot is open. The PR has one unresolved review thread whose newest comment is a human question with no muggle-do:bot marker, but GitHub reports isOutdated=true on the thread because a later push moved the line it was anchored to. CI is green and the branch is level with master. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: treats_outdated_thread_as_actionable
assertions.text: Plan marks the thread actionable even though isOutdated=true — the gates are resolution state and the loop marker, never outdatedness.

assertions.name: does_not_skip_on_isOutdated
assertions.text: Plan does NOT skip or idle the thread on the grounds that its anchored line moved; the unanswered question survives the line move and must be surfaced.

assertions.name: dispatches_address_reviews
assertions.text: Plan dispatches /muggle-do with an address-reviews directive for the thread's owning review id, rather than idling.

assertions.name: leaves_mootness_to_mdo
assertions.text: Plan leaves the judgment of whether the moved code already mooted the concern to /muggle-do's reply — it is not a reason for the watcher to filter the thread out.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr510 510. The slot is open. The PR has one unresolved review thread with isOutdated=true whose newest comment carries the muggle-do:bot marker — the loop has already replied. CI is green and the branch is level with master. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: marker_makes_it_non_actionable
assertions.text: Plan treats the thread as non-actionable because its newest comment carries the muggle-do:bot marker — the marker rule holds regardless of outdatedness.

assertions.name: no_dispatch_no_echo
assertions.text: Plan does NOT dispatch address-reviews; re-dispatching would echo the loop's own reply.

assertions.name: idles_transiently
assertions.text: Plan idles this tick as a transient idle (green, branch current, awaiting the next human comment) and keeps the 1m cadence — it is not a durable human-block.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr520 520 — this fire was delivered by a /loop recovery cron, not a monitor wake. The slot is open, watch-heartbeat was touched 40 seconds ago, there are no unresolved review threads, CI is green, and the branch is level with master. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: recognises_cron_delivered_fire
assertions.text: Plan recognises this tick was delivered by a /loop recovery cron and therefore runs the hand-back-to-monitor step — a monitor wake or a headless watchdog tick would skip it.

assertions.name: reads_heartbeat_as_live_monitor
assertions.text: Plan reads watch-heartbeat mtime, sees it is fresh (within 3 minutes), and concludes a live monitor already owns the 1m cadence.

assertions.name: cancels_duplicate_cron
assertions.text: Plan cancels this cron per cancel-cron.md (recorded-id first) because it is a duplicate poller — there is nothing to arm.

assertions.name: never_recreates_cron_or_double_arms
assertions.text: Plan does NOT CronCreate a recurring cron and does NOT start a second monitor over the live one; exactly one poller (the monitor) remains.

evals.prompt: Tick muggle-ai-works-pr521 521 — this fire was delivered by a /loop recovery cron. The slot is open, watch-heartbeat is missing (the last monitor died), there are no unresolved review threads, CI is green, and the branch is level with master. Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: detects_dead_monitor_from_beacon
assertions.text: Plan reads watch-heartbeat, finds it missing or older than 3 minutes, and concludes the monitor is dead and this cron has become the primary poller.

assertions.name: finishes_arming_a_monitor
assertions.text: Plan finishes the arm-watcher sequence — seed the watermark from a fresh post-tick fetch, start the persistent labeled monitor, ensure the watchdog — using this tick as the drain.

assertions.name: cancels_cron_after_arming
assertions.text: Plan then cancels this cron per cancel-cron.md and appends a re-armed (monitor restored) line to followup.log, so the 1m cadence lives in the token-free monitor rather than a per-minute model turn.

assertions.name: never_rearms_with_a_cron
assertions.text: Plan does NOT restore the poller by creating a recurring /loop cron; the cron is only ever a one-shot recovery delivery.

evals.prompt: Reconcile the slots. muggle-ai-works-pr522 522 is open (no result.md), but its watch-heartbeat is 40 minutes stale and the newest followup.log line is 40 minutes old — the watcher stopped silently (a crashed cycle that never respawned). The global kill file is absent. Walk me through the plan for this slot.

assertions.name: classifies_silent_watcher_from_freshest_beacon
assertions.text: Plan judges the watcher dead because the freshest beacon (watch-heartbeat mtime or newest followup.log line) is older than the staleness window.

assertions.name: rearms_via_arm_watcher_monitor
assertions.text: Plan re-arms per arm-watcher.md — drain tick, watermark seed, persistent monitor, watchdog ensure — restoring a token-free poller.

assertions.name: never_rearms_with_cron
assertions.text: Plan does NOT re-arm by creating a recurring /loop cron; the 1m cadence belongs in the monitor and a cron fire would be a full model turn.

assertions.name: would_skip_under_killfile
assertions.text: Plan notes it would skip re-arming entirely if polling.disabled existed — here it is absent, so it proceeds.

evals.prompt: The owner runs stop for muggle-ai-works-pr523 523 (one slot). The slot has a live monitor, a recorded cron id in cron.json, and on Windows an inner bash watch.sh grandchild. Walk me through the plan.

assertions.name: stops_monitor_including_windows_grandchild
assertions.text: Plan TaskStops the monitor AND kills the surviving bash <slug>/watch.sh grandchild (enumerated by command line) that outlives TaskStop on Windows — otherwise it keeps touching watch-heartbeat and its open handles block the rename.

assertions.name: cancels_cron_recorded_id_first
assertions.text: Plan cancels the cron per cancel-cron.md, recorded-id first with a CronList-match fallback, and admits a cron neither lookup reaches is orphaned but inert.

assertions.name: renames_slot_to_stopped
assertions.text: Plan renames the slot dir to <slug>.stopped — the load-bearing act the tick absorb, reconcile, and the watchdog all key on to stay away.

assertions.name: no_global_killfile_for_single_slot
assertions.text: Plan does NOT write the global polling.disabled kill file for a scoped single-slot stop, and writes no result.md — stopping is resumable, not finalizing.

evals.prompt: The owner runs stop with no slug — take every watcher down. Several slots are open with live monitors and recorded crons. Walk me through the plan.

assertions.name: stops_and_renames_every_open_slot
assertions.text: Plan stops each open slot (monitor + Windows grandchild + cron) and renames each to <slug>.stopped.

assertions.name: writes_global_killfile
assertions.text: Plan writes the global kill file ~/.muggle-ai/muggle-do/polling.disabled so any surviving orphaned cron fire absorbs itself before resolving a slot, and reconcile refuses to re-arm while it exists.

assertions.name: stopping_is_not_finalizing
assertions.text: Plan writes no result.md — a stopped slot stays open on the provider and is resumable by renaming <slug>.stopped back and re-arming.

assertions.name: honest_about_orphan_floor
assertions.text: Plan reports an orphaned cron honestly — it may keep firing one-line absorbs until its host session ends, which is the harness's floor, not a teardown failure.

evals.prompt: Tick agent-pin-conversions 137 — this fire was delivered by an orphaned /loop cron whose handle a compaction severed. On disk the live slot is gone and only agent-pin-conversions.stopped exists (the owner ran stop). Walk me through the plan for this tick.

assertions.name: absorbs_before_any_fetch_or_write
assertions.text: Plan checks for the .stopped slot (and the polling.disabled kill file) at the very top of Step 0, before any GitHub fetch, state write, or log line.

assertions.name: one_line_absorb_then_exit
assertions.text: Plan outputs a single line (stopped: <slug> — absorbed) and exits — no fetch, no state write, no followup.log line, no dispatch.

assertions.name: does_not_resurrect_or_guess_delete
assertions.text: Plan does NOT recreate the slot, re-arm a monitor, or delete cron ids CronList surfaces for other slugs — those belong to other live watchers.

assertions.name: absorb_caps_the_orphan
assertions.text: Plan recognises this absorb gate is exactly what caps an unreachable orphaned cron at one harmless line per fire until its session dies.

evals.prompt: Bootstrap a watcher from the URL https://github.com/multiplex-ai/muggle-ai-works/pull/524. The global polling.disabled kill file is present from an earlier stop-everything. Walk me through the plan.

assertions.name: clears_killfile_as_first_act
assertions.text: Plan deletes the polling.disabled kill file during bootstrap, treating a pasted PR URL as an explicit request to watch that overrides a prior stop-everything.

assertions.name: surfaces_the_clear_in_one_line
assertions.text: Plan says in one line that it cleared the kill file, so the state change is visible.

assertions.name: then_seeds_and_arms
assertions.text: Plan then seeds the slot and arms the watch normally — leaving the kill file in place would make every tick of the new watch absorb itself stillborn.

assertions.name: only_bootstrap_clears_it
assertions.text: Plan notes only bootstrap (an explicit URL) clears the kill file; auto-track and reconcile never do.
